The '''24th Academy Awards''' were held on March 20, 1952, honoring the films from [[1951 in film|1951]] and the ceremony was hosted by [[Danny Kaye]].

''[[An American in Paris (film)|An American in Paris]]'' and ''[[A Place in the Sun (1951 film)|A Place in the Sun]]'' each received six Oscars, splitting [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], respectively. ''[[A Streetcar Named Desire (1951 film)|A Streetcar Named Desire]]'' won four Oscars, including [[List of films with all four Academy Award acting nominations|three of the four acting awards]] for which it was nominated. The film's only unsuccessful acting nomination was that of [[Marlon Brando]], whose performance as [[Stanley Kowalski]] was later considered one of the most influential of modern film acting.<ref>{{cite news
 |url=http://rogerebert.suntimes.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/19931112/REVIEWS/311120304/1023

 |archive-date=2005-04-13 
}}</ref><!--ref>{{cite web

[[Humphrey Bogart]] was the last man born in the 19th century to win [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]]. He won it over favored winner Marlon Brando, by the logic of the former being too long overlooked and the latter being a newcomer.<ref name="Oscars '51 Notes"/> The next day, Bogart remarked that "awards don't mean a thing unless every actor plays [[Hamlet]] and then who is best is decided."<ref name="Oscars '51 Notes"/>

''[[An American in Paris (film)|An American in Paris]]'' became the second color film to win Best Picture, and was the first film since ''[[Grand Hotel (1932 film)|Grand Hotel]]'' to win Best Picture without any acting nominations.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shaw |first1=Gabbi |title='Parasite' is the 12th movie in history to win Best Picture with no acting nominations — here are the other 11 |url=https://www.insider.com/movies-that-won-best-picture-oscars-with-no-acting-nominations |website=Insider |publisher=Insider Inc. |access-date=27 March 2023}}</ref> Its win was a surprise, as either ''[[A Streetcar Named Desire (1951 film)|A Streetcar Named Desire]]'' or ''[[A Place in the Sun (1951 film)|A Place in the Sun]]'' was expected to win. Some reflected that it may have won due to the number of Academy voters employed by [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]] at the time.<ref name="Oscars '51 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/838/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=839 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref>

===Best Special Effects===
* ''[[When Worlds Collide (1951 film)|When Worlds Collide]]'' – [[Paramount Pictures|Paramount]].

===Honorary Foreign Language Film Award===
*To ''[[Rashomon]]'' - voted by the Board of Governors as the most outstanding foreign language film released in the United States during 1951.

===Honorary Award===
*To [[Gene Kelly]] in appreciation of his versatility as an actor, singer, director and dancer, and specifically for his brilliant achievements in the art of choreography on film.

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
*[[Arthur Freed]]
